response.sql: WITH execution_counts AS (SELECT o.ordertune, COUNT(DISTINCT o.orderspivot) as count FROM orderexecutions oe INNER JOIN orders o ON oe.ordersmark = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.ordertune), total_info AS (SELECT SUM(count) as total_count, COUNT(*) as num_types FROM execution_counts), shares AS (SELECT ec.ordertune, ec.count, CAST(ec.count AS REAL) / ti.total_count as share, 1.0 / ti.num_types as avg_share FROM execution_counts ec CROSS JOIN total_info ti), filtered_shares AS (SELECT * FROM shares WHERE share > avg_share) SELECT SUM(count) as sum_of_counts, AVG(share) as avg_share_of_filtered, AVG(share - avg_share) as avg_excess_over_avg FROM filtered_shares

assumptions.assumption: "Executed orders" counts distinct orders per type that received at least one execution, not individual execution records. The phrase "how many executed orders" reads as counting order entities rather than fill records.
NULL order types are treated as a distinct group (GROUP BY naturally groups NULLs together).

alternatives.interpretation: Count individual execution/fill records for each order type instead of distinct orders. This counts multiple fills of the same order separately.
alternatives.sql: WITH execution_counts AS (SELECT o.ordertune, COUNT(*) as count FROM orderexecutions oe INNER JOIN orders o ON oe.ordersmark = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.ordertune), total_info AS (SELECT SUM(count) as total_count, COUNT(*) as num_types FROM execution_counts), shares AS (SELECT ec.ordertune, ec.count, CAST(ec.count AS REAL) / ti.total_count as share, 1.0 / ti.num_types as avg_share FROM execution_counts ec CROSS JOIN total_info ti), filtered_shares AS (SELECT * FROM shares WHERE share > avg_share) SELECT SUM(count) as sum_of_counts, AVG(share) as avg_share_of_filtered, AVG(share - avg_share) as avg_excess_over_avg FROM filtered_shares
